prerequisites: Good knowledge of the fundamental principles of signal theory, with particular reference to the spectral analysis of deterministic signals and stochastic processes.
Knowledge of the basic mathematical tools used in the analysis of linear systems.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire fundamental knowledge of the operating principles of telecommunication systems, including digital modulation, characterization and modeling of noise, signal reception techniques in the presence of noise and interference, and basic principles of equalization for compensating channel distortions.
Acquire theoretical tools required to understand, model, and analyze the main telecommunication systems operating both at baseband and in passband.
Model and analyze analog and digital communication systems operating both at baseband and in passband.
Compare different communication systems in terms of spectral efficiency, energy efficiency, and overall performance.
Represent and assess the effects of distortions and impairments introduced by the transmission channel on the received signal.

Select the most appropriate transmission technique according to system requirements, such as data transmission rate and bit error probability, and the available resources, such as bandwidth and transmit power.
Apply the analysis methods learned to the evaluation of simple telecommunication systems in practical contexts.

syllabus_topics: Characterization of Noise in Communication Systems
Power spectral density dissipated on a load
Available power spectral density of a generator
Available power gain of a two-port network
Nyquist theorem for noisy linear networks
Equivalent noise temperature and noise figure
Friis formula
Equivalent noise bandwidth
Communication systems over radio and cable channels
Repeaters for analog and digital signals
Analog-to-Digital Conversion of a Signal
PCM technique: uniform and non-uniform quantization
Compressor and expander
Sample interpolation
Performance of a PCM system: quantization noise and effect of transmission channel errors
Performance curves of PCM systems
Theory of Digital Modulations
PAM modulation: analytical signal model and its power spectral density
Structure of modulator and demodulator
Nyquist condition for intersymbol interference (ISI) elimination
Design of transmit and receive filters
Raised cosine pulses
QAM and PSK modulations: analytical signal model and its power spectral density
Structure of modulator and demodulator
Effect of phase error in carrier reconstruction
Decision regions and bit error probability calculation
Channel Equalization Techniques
Wireless channel model: multipath propagation
Coherence bandwidth and coherence time
Statistical models of indoor, typical urban, and hilly terrain channels
Linear equalizers in the time domain
Criteria for setting equalizer coefficients: Zero-Forcing and Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE)
Performance of equalization techniques
teaching_methods: Microsoft Teams platform for materials and announcements
Active student participation through questions, contributions, discussions
assessment_rules: The examination consists of an oral test covering main topics including analog and digital modulation, analog-to-digital signal conversion, channel equalization techniques, and noise effects. Students will be assessed on theoretical understanding, application of concepts, clarity of presentation, and technical terminology. They may also solve and discuss exercises, potentially in written form during the oral examination. The exam is passed if the student demonstrates adequate command of fundamental concepts, ability to reason and connect topics, and clarity and rigor in presentation.
